chapters.reason: The paper introduces Gated Linear Attention (GLA) Transformers, which replace standard self-attention with a linear attention mechanism to achieve subquadratic complexity, directly aligning with the description of subquadratic attention.

The paper evaluates GLA Transformers on language modeling tasks, demonstrating competitive performance against models like LLaMA, RetNet, and Mamba, which involves applying subquadratic attention architectures to reasoning-related tasks (though not explicitly CoT).

The paper discusses linear attention as enabling efficient inference by formulating it as an RNN, which relates to converting transformer-like structures into linear recurrent forms for deployment efficiency, though it is not a conversion of a pretrained transformer.
